headline: No 64–68 water on the chart — Friday, west corner, or wait
body:
Fog is the hazard, not wind: patchy dense fog this morning with visibility a mile or less across the channel and outer waters, and patchy fog again Saturday morning. No small-craft advisory. Friday inside the channel is light early, west 10–15 by afternoon, seas 2–3 ft at the harbor and about 3 ft in the triangle. Saturday is softer still — 2 ft inshore, 2.7 ft in the triangle, light southwest winds until a late west breeze.

Be honest about the water: nothing on the chart is in the 64–68 band. The triangle reads 70.4 at the west corner, 71.2 at the south point, 71.5 south of Anacapa Friday, and everything warms a degree Saturday. The break has slid off the zone entirely. If you go, go Friday and work the west corner and the west–south edge on that 70.4, looking for bait and any cooler edge.

Santa Rosa Flats is the coolest water at 69.1, but still over 68 and lumpy at 4.5 ft with northwest 14 gusting 15 — not worth the run. Osborn and San Nicolas are warmer yet. Neither day is a true bluefin day.
